seo.metaTitle: Add Text to PNG - Free Image Text Tool, No Upload
seo.metaDescription: Draw a text label on a PNG in your browser: font, size, color, bold, a position on a 3x3 grid and an optional backing plate. Free, no upload.
seo.longDescription: Add text to PNG draws a text label straight onto the pixels — the right tool for a caption on a mockup, a date on a photo or a single watermark. Pick the font family, size, weight and color, choose one of nine positions around the frame, set the margin from the edge, and switch on a semi-transparent backing plate when the picture behind is too busy. The text is rendered by the browser on your device, so the image never leaves it.
facts: Runs entirely in your browser: no upload, no server, no signup.
One label in one of nine positions — for a repeated pattern use the watermark tile tool.
Optional semi-transparent backing plate for busy backgrounds.
The picture is not resampled; saving as PNG or WebP keeps the rest lossless.
Free with no daily limit, no watermark and no account, also for commercial use.
howTo: Drop the image into the source area, or pick a file from your device.
Type the text, then set the font, size, bold and color.
Choose a position on the 3x3 grid and set the margin from the edge.
Turn on the plate and tune its color and opacity if the text needs contrast.
Download the result from the Download button.

faq.a: It draws a single label at a chosen position. For a repeated pattern across the whole picture, use the watermark tile tool on this site instead.

faq.q: Why is my text hard to read?
faq.a: Turn on the backing plate and lower its opacity until the text reads without looking like a sticker, or place the label over a quieter part of the picture by moving the margin.

The browser fonts on your system - a sans-serif and a monospace family are offered. Because the rendering happens locally, the look depends on the fonts installed on the device, which is also why an uploaded PNG always looks the same everywhere.

faq.q: Does adding text reduce image quality?
faq.a: The picture is not resampled - the label is drawn on top of the original pixels, and saving as PNG or WebP keeps the rest of the image lossless.
